title: Repeat-Record Credit on Seller Performance Standing Clean-Span Relief
content:
**Credit.** The repeat-record credit of clean-span relief is the no-repeat credit of 2 points for a seller with no violation type recorded more than once in the last twelve whole calendar months, the single-repeat credit of 1 point for a seller with a type recorded twice in that period and none more often, and nothing for a seller with a type recorded three or more times in that period.

The credit applies to clean-span relief under Seller Performance Standing. It is added to the relief points after they have been rounded down to a whole point, and the total so formed is what the clean-span relief cap limits.

## Reading the violation history

The six violation types are listing policy, restricted product, intellectual property, inauthentic complaint, product authenticity and review manipulation. For each type, the violations of that type recorded in the last twelve whole calendar months are counted — a violation lies in that period when fewer than twelve whole months have passed from its recording date to the handling date, counted by calendar date. The type with the highest count decides the credit.

| Highest count of any one type in the period | Credit |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 2 points |
| 2 | 1 point |
| 3 or more | none |

## Cases (hypothetical histories over the last twelve whole calendar months)

| Violations recorded | Highest single-type count | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| one listing policy, one restricted product, one intellectual property | 1 | 2 |
| two listing policy, one restricted product | 2 | 1 |
| two listing policy, two restricted product | 2 | 1 |
| three listing policy | 3 | none |
| none | 0 | 2 |

**Worked figure.** Relief points rounded down to 3, with a credit of 1, total 4 before the cap is applied.
